dosing_regimen.source_excerpt: protocolSection.armsInterventionsModule and protocolSection.descriptionModule.detailedDescription: "In Part A1, eligible participants were randomized at Baseline at a ratio of 4:1, stratified by weight and prior exposure to tumor necrosis factor antagonists to receive double-blind (DB) risankizumab 150 mg or placebo at Weeks 0 and 4." "In Part A2, participants randomized at Baseline to receive DB placebo then received risankizumab 150 mg at Weeks 16 (Part A2) and at Week 28 and every 12 weeks up to 88 weeks (Part B); participants randomized to risankizumab 150 mg continued to receive risankizumab 150 mg at Week 16." "Participants who received risankizumab in Part A and were nonresponders (sPGA \>2) at Week 28 received risankizumab 150 mg at Week 28 and every 12 weeks up to 88 weeks (Part B)." "In Part B, participants who received risankizumab in Part A and were responders (sPGA ≤2) at Week 28, were rerandomized at a ratio of 1:2 to receive DB risankizumab 150 mg or placebo at Week 28 and every 12 weeks up to 88 weeks (Part B)." "Starting at Week 32, rerandomized participants who reached relapse (defined as sPGA ≥3) were switched to risankizumab 150 mg every 12 weeks." "Participants randomized at Baseline to receive double-blind (DB) risankizumab 150 mg by subcutaneous injection at Weeks 0 and 4 (Part A1)." "Participants randomized at Baseline to receive double-blind (DB) placebo by subcutaneous injection at Weeks 0 and 4 (Part A1)." "Risankizumab administered by subcutaneous injection" "Placebo for risankizumab administered by subcutaneous injection" -- The intervention descriptions are copied unchanged from CT.gov. Risankizumab is explicitly subcutaneous; Part A1 gives 150 mg or matching placebo at Weeks 0 and 4. Subsequent registry text describes the Week 16 transition and Part B dosing every 12 weeks through Week 88, with relapse-triggered switching to risankizumab. Because schedules change across parts and arms, frequency and dosing_periods are left null/empty rather than merging arm-specific schedules. Dose form is represented as injection from the explicit administration route; no unit count is stated.

severity_criteria.source_excerpt: protocolSection.eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria; sPGA outcome definition: "* Have stable moderate to severe chronic plaque psoriasis with or without psoriatic arthritis at both Screening and Baseline (Randomization); Have an involved body surface area (BSA) ≥ 10% and Have a Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI) ≥ 12 and Have a static Physician Global Assessment (sPGA) score of ≥ 3." "The sPGA ranges from 0 to 4, and is calculated as Clear (0) = 0 for all three; Almost clear (1) = mean \>0, \<1.5; Mild (2) = mean ≥1.5, \<2.5; Moderate (3) = mean ≥2.5, \<3.5; and Severe (4) = mean ≥3.5." -- The inclusion text explicitly calls the condition stable moderate to severe plaque psoriasis and requires BSA >=10%, PASI >=12, and sPGA >=3 at screening and baseline. The sPGA definition states a 0-to-4 range.

prohibited_concomitant: Guselkumab and tildrakizumab were not allowed before or during trial participation.

The protocol lists specified systemic psoriasis therapies, phototherapy, and psoriasis topicals as restricted, with pre-randomization washout durations and restrictions through the end-of-observation visit.
permitted_concomitant: Stable doses of concomitant therapies for chronic conditions were permissible when neither the condition nor treatment excluded participation.
Symptomatic therapy for adverse events was permitted at investigator judgment.
value.population_note: The protocol supports chronic-condition concomitant therapy and specified prohibited/restricted medication classes, but does not establish a monotherapy design or a standardized background regimen. Restrictions include pre-randomization washout periods; those durations are not represented as during-treatment prohibitions here.

multiplicity_control.source_excerpt: SAP Sections 10.2 and 10.3 ranked efficacy analyses; Section 10.4 Handling of Multiplicity: "● Achievement of ≥ 90% reduction from baseline PASI score (PASI 90) at" "Week 16" "● Achievement of an sPGA of clear or almost clear (0 or 1) at Week 16" "The achievement of PASI 90 at Week 16 is the first co-primary endpoint." "The achievement of a sPGA of clear or almost clear at Week 16 is the second co-primary" "The co-primary endpoints of PASI 90 and sPGA clear or almost clear need to be" "Both endpoints will be tested using a two-sided test with a" "type I error rate of 0.05." "The ranked secondary endpoints in Part A are in ranked order as follows:" "Achievement of ≥ 75% reduction from baseline PASI score (PASI 75) at Week 16" "Achievement of 100% reduction from baseline PASI score (PASI 100) at Week 16" "Achievement of sPGA of clear at Week 16" "Achievement of DLQI score of 0 or 1 at Week 16" "hypotheses will be tested in a hierarchical order using two-sided tests with a type I error" "of 0.05 only if the null hypothesis for the co-primary endpoints in Part A1 has been" "significant results (P value ≤ 0.05) for the comparison in the higher rank (primary, then" "ranked secondary variables) are necessary to initiate the testing of the next comparison in" "the lower rank." "Since a step-down procedure is used, each comparison will be tested at a" "significance level of 0.05 and overall alpha level of 0.05 will be preserved." "2." "3." "4." "40" -- The two co-primary endpoints must both be significant (simultaneous tests, two-sided alpha 0.05). The four ranked Week 16 secondary endpoints follow in the stated order after the co-primary nulls are rejected. The SAP says step-down procedure and overall alpha 0.05 is preserved; no available procedure enum exactly represents that method, so procedure is null. The SAP does not explicitly state finalization. The integer alpha_sided=2 is the schema encoding of the SAP wording two-sided; testing-sequence step values 2, 3, and 4 are supported by the numbered ranked list (the extracted sequence order is explicit). Overall alpha preservation is stated explicitly in SAP:1607, and ranked secondary testing only after rejection of the co-primary nulls is stated in SAP:1508.

permitted_concomitant: Rescue treatment when the investigator deems psoriasis increase intolerable; the patient is discontinued from the trial to receive it.
value.applies_to_period: During the trial; rescue results in trial discontinuation.
value.rationale: Protocol permits rescue treatment at investigator judgment for an intolerable increase in psoriasis, with discontinuation from the trial. This is distinct from the protocol-defined relapse and open-label retreatment after Week 28.

rescue_therapy.source_excerpt: 4.2.1 Rescue medication, emergency procedures, and additional treatment(s): "If the patient experiences an intolerable increase of psoriasis during the course of the trial as" "deemed by the investigator, the patient will be discontinued from the trial to receive rescue" "treatment." "In case of adverse events in need of treatment symptomatic therapy according to investigator" "judgment will be permitted." -- Only the rescue rule expressly described in Section 4.2.1 is extracted. The response-triggered retreatment after Week 28 is described separately in the schedule and is not classified as rescue.

published_results.source_excerpt: 14.1 Clinical Trials in Subjects with Moderate-to-Severe Plaque Psoriasis, Trial PsO-3: "Percent of Adult Subjects with Active Psoriatic Arthritis Achieving ACR20 Responses in Trial PsA-1 through Week 24 14.1 Clinical Trials in Subjects with Moderate-to-Severe Plaque Psoriasis Adults with Moderate-to-Severe Plaque Psoriasis Four multicenter, randomized, double-blind trials [PsO-1 (NCT02684370), PsO-2 (NCT02684357), PsO-3 (NCT02672852), and PsO-4 (NCT02694523)] enrolled 2,109 subjects 18 years of age and older with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis who had a body surface area (BSA) involvement of ≥10%, a static Physician’s Global Assessment (sPGA) score of ≥3 (" "Trial PsO-3 Trial PsO-3 enrolled 507 subjects (407 randomized to SKYRIZI 150 mg and 100 to placebo)." "At Week 16, SKYRIZI was superior to placebo on the co-primary endpoints of sPGA 0 or 1 (84% SKYRIZI and 7% placebo) and PASI 90 (73% SKYRIZI and 2% placebo)." -- The label identifies PsO-3 as NCT02672852, reports 407 subjects randomized to SKYRIZI and 100 to placebo, and gives Week 16 co-primary response rates. Values are printed percentages; responder counts are not back-calculated. The label section is adult plaque psoriasis and reports these arm-level trial results at Week 16.
